name: Travis Nelson
occupation: State Representative; registered nurse and union representative

bio.statement: In his official biography Nelson says he joined the legislature as the first Black LGBTQIA+ member of the body.
bio.excerpt: I am proud to join the legislature as the first ever Black LGBTQIA+ member of this body

source.publisher: Oregon Legislature, Rep. Nelson member page

bio.statement: The Oregon Capital Chronicle reported at his appointment that Nelson is a registered nurse working as a union representative with the Oregon Nurses Association.
bio.excerpt: Nelson is a registered nurse who now works full time as a union representative with the Oregon Nurses Association.

source.publisher: Oregon Capital Chronicle

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists Nelson's occupation as registered nurse, labor representative and State Representative, with a background as Oregon Nurses Association vice president, ER and ICU nurse, coach and janitor.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Registered Nurse, Labor Representative, State Representative Occupational Background: Oregon Nurses Association Vice President, ER Nurse, ICU Nurse, Coach, Janitor

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists Washington State University and Columbia Basin College as his educational background.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: Washington State University, Columbia Basin College

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists State Representative since 2022, Vice Chair of the Legislative BI-POC Caucus, and service on the Oregon Pain Commission Board and Commission on Black Affairs as prior governmental experience.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: State Representative since 2022, Vice Chair Legislative BI-POC Caucus, Legislative Environmental Caucus Member, Oregon Pain Commission Board, Oregon Commission on Black Affairs

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

positions.statement: Nelson's pamphlet statement lists housing for all as a priority: expanding affordable housing, addressing homelessness, and supporting mental health and addiction recovery services.
positions.excerpt: Housing for All: Expanding affordable housing, addressing homelessness, and supporting mental health and addiction recovery services.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

positions.statement: Nelson lists healthcare for all as a priority in his pamphlet statement: lower costs, a stronger workforce and safe hospital staffing.
positions.excerpt: Healthcare for All: Lowering healthcare costs, strengthening the healthcare workforce, and safe staffing in hospitals.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

positions.statement: Nelson's pamphlet statement lists fully funding education and ensuring every student has a safe and supportive learning environment.
positions.excerpt: Support for Schools: Fully funding education and ensuring every student has a safe and supportive learning environment.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement Nelson says he is the first Black, LGBTQ+ member of the state legislature and brings a voice not historically heard.
positions.excerpt: Equity: I’m the first Black, LGBTQ+ member of the state legislature. I bring a voice that hasn’t historically been heard.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

positions.statement: Nelson says in his pamphlet statement that he passed legislation protecting abortion rights and gender-affirming care and is advocating for a universal healthcare plan.
positions.excerpt: Reproductive Healthcare: Passed legislation to protect abortion rights & gender-affirming care.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

positions.statement: Nelson's pamphlet statement cites legislation strengthening child labor protections and says he continues to fight for fair wages and safe workplaces.
positions.excerpt: Protecting Workers: Passed legislation strengthening child labor protections. I continue fighting for fair wages and safe workplaces.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

positions.statement: Nelson's pamphlet statement cites funding for North and Northeast Portland, including the Albina Vision Trust redevelopment, George Park and $15 million for a future North Portland Aquatic Center.
positions.excerpt: Local Investments: Secured millions for North and Northeast Portland, including investments in the Albina Vision Trust redevelopment, improvements to George Park, $15 million for a future North Portland Aquatic Center

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 53

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Nelson says nobody should have to sleep outside and that housing people makes it easier to connect them with services.
positions.excerpt: Nobody should have to sleep outside. Making sure people are housed makes it much easier to connect them with services.

source.publisher: Travis Nelson campaign website (nelsonfororegon.com)

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Nelson says Oregon has been a national leader in creating climate goals.
positions.excerpt: Oregon has been a national leader in creating climate goals.

source.publisher: Travis Nelson campaign website (nelsonfororegon.com)

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Nelson says public higher education should open doors rather than saddle young people with lifelong debt.
positions.excerpt: Public higher education should open doors, not saddle young people with lifelong debt.

source.publisher: Travis Nelson campaign website (nelsonfororegon.com)
